The proposal schema maps one bronze column to one silver action with no merge action, so year, month, and day stay as three INTEGER columns rather than the single DATE column the operator's convention calls for; a downstream transform can combine them later.

purpose: This silver table is the cleaned record of NYC flight departures from nycflights13 covering January-June 2013, feeding downstream flight-delay, punctuality, and route analyses.
usage: Consumers should treat departure_time, arrival_time, departure_delay_minutes, arrival_delay_minutes, and air_time_minutes as nullable because flights that never departed or arrived carry no recorded value in these fields; filter on departure_time IS NOT NULL when only completed flights are needed. The HHMM time fields (departure_time, scheduled_departure_time, arrival_time, scheduled_arrival_time, hour, minute) remain integers in the source's local-time encoding, not true TIME values, so parse them deliberately before any temporal join. scheduled_hour_utc is a true UTC TIMESTAMP and can be joined directly to other UTC time series.
limitations: year, month, and day remain three separate INTEGER columns rather than the single DATE column the operator's naming convention calls for, because the proposal schema maps one bronze column to exactly one silver action; a later transform should combine them. tail_number is null for about 0.9% of rows (1521 of 166158), and the departure/arrival time, delay, and air-time columns are null for roughly 3% of rows (departure_time 2.94%, arrival_time 3.07%, arrival_delay_minutes 3.30%), corresponding to flights that never departed or arrived; these nulls are retained rather than imputed. No exact duplicate rows were found (duplicate_row_rate 0.0 across 166158 rows), so no dedupe logic was applied.
